sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 34.8% a year from $404.5 million in FY2016 to $5,931.4 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
The shape is a decelerating growth curve: 64.2% in FY2021, 11.8% in FY2022, 0.1% in FY2023, then 16.4% and 10.6% in FY2024 and FY2025 [D218][D263][D311][D358][D406].
FY2017's operating loss of $3,485.6 million was driven by a $2.6 billion increase in stock-based compensation, primarily the CEO award and IPO performance RSUs [F12][P74].
The FY2022 reversal to a $1,395.3 million operating loss came from higher cost of revenue and operating expenses, partly offset by revenue [F17][P42].
Since then the loss has narrowed every year, to $532.2 million in FY2025, an operating margin of -9.0% against a window median of -32.4% [F20][F30][D555].
North America remains the largest market at 58.6% of FY2025 revenue but contributed only 4.4pp of the 10.6% growth [D456][D458][D406].
Other revenue, mostly subscriptions, grew 62.9% and contributed 5.4pp, nearly matching advertising's 5.3pp on 5.8% growth [D544][D545][D537][D538].
Advertising growth came from roughly 17% more impressions, largely via Sponsored Snaps and Spotlight, partly offset by a 10% lower cost per impression; other revenue rose on subscriber growth [P24].
Operating costs grew 5.1% against 10.6% revenue growth, so the incremental operating margin was 44.8% [D423][D406][D429].
The diluted share count rose 2.1% in FY2025, so the loss per share fell 35.7% against a 34.0% fall in net loss [D425][D410][D408].
The FY2025 operating margin of -9.0% is the window high, far above the -422.5% low in FY2017 [F30][D553][D554].
Cost of revenue added 1.1pp and R&D 1.3pp to the margin, other lines added 3.3pp, and the operating margin rose 5.7pp to -9.0% [D431][D432][D433][D419][F30].
Sales and marketing fell $42.4 million on the timing of marketing events, lower advertising, and prior-year restructuring charges [P22].
R&D rose $101.9 million on product development and headcount, and G&A rose $60.0 million on external professional services including legal [P23][P21].
Net margin of -7.8% sits 1.2pp above operating margin, helped by $96.7 million of debt-extinguishment gains in other income [F50][F30][D591][P18].
Operating cash flow of $656.2 million and free cash flow of $437.2 million in FY2025 both exceed the $460.5 million net loss [F80][F100][F40].
Operating cash flow was driven by the net loss adjusted for $1.0 billion of stock-based compensation and $163.6 million of D&A, plus working-capital timing [P13].
Free cash flow margin reached 7.4%, a window high against a -4.1% median, with capex at 3.7% of revenue and 1.34x D&A [D393][D561][D392][D395].
Capex of $219.0 million was primarily improvements to leased facilities to support team workspaces [P10].
Cash and investments of $2,940.6 million against total debt of $3,536.8 million left net debt of $596.3 million, or -10.1% of revenue [D397][D398][D399][D400].
That net cash position ranks at the 0th percentile against internet peers (n=5), whose median is 45.0% of revenue [D578][D579].
In February 2025 Snap issued $1.50 billion of 2033 Notes and repurchased $1.4 billion of 2026, 2027 and 2028 Notes, producing a $66.9 million gain [P2][P1].
Buybacks of $750.9 million were 171.7% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count still rose 2.1% [D401][D402][D425].
Snap has posted a net loss in each of the last ten years, from $514.6 million in FY2016 to $460.5 million in FY2025 [R1][F31][F40].
Stock-based compensation was 17.1% of revenue in FY2025 and at least 10% in each of the last nine years [R2][D390].
Net cash has fallen for four straight years, from $1,439.8 million in FY2021 to net debt of $596.3 million in FY2025 [R3][D211][D399].
Buybacks exceeded free cash flow in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, at 544.3%, 142.3% and 171.7% [R4][D307][D354][D402].
Operating margin: a FY2026 reading above the FY2025 -9.0% would extend the narrowing trend, while a move back toward the -32.4% median would reverse it [F30][D555].
Free cash flow margin: holding above the FY2025 7.4% high would confirm the cash trend; falling below the -4.1% median would break it [D393][D561].
Net cash: a return above zero from the FY2025 -$596.3 million would reverse the four-year slide, reported in the FY2026 10-K [D399].
